Well, where did you hear music? Where did you hear music in those days?

Oh, I used to go to all the dances here. Artesian Hall, the Frans Amé, the Globe. There's several different dance halls. I mean, they still got the Frans Amé here, didn't they? Of course, I haven't been dancing so long. Later. Economy? Economy Hall, yeah. Yeah, the economy. Artesian? Artesian, Frans Amé. Clothes. What's that? Yeah, St. Jean-Louis. Where my niece got married there. That's back there. St. Jean-Louis? Yeah, it's back with Calouret Street. Somewhere in Calouret Street. There was Ramport, somewhere in that section. There was Ramport, there was Ramport. That's how we went over there, wasn't that? Then we'd go there meet you and, uh, the club named Bichy. No, they got the Newhall, they got the autographs. The autographs give it to the jolly boys around the corner. They give dances there, aren't you? Yeah.
The Bichy had the birthday party every minute.
Yeah. Yeah.
He played there. He played too. Yeah. The Yorval Room.
The Alliance Club, the Santa Cendez. It's still, I don't know if Santa Cendez still have dance, I don't know. The club is still there.

segments.title: Opening: names, address and Paul Crawford on the recorder
segments.summary: Allen opens the tape at 1619 North Galveston and has Billie, De De, Silver Trepagnier and Paul Crawford give their names.

segments.title: Billie's age and her parents' hymn playing
segments.summary: Billie says she was born in 1907, that her mother and father played piano and sang hymns in a Baptist choir, and that the children grew up on ragtime.

segments.title: Billie's seven sisters and who read music
segments.summary: She names her sisters, praises Mabel and Sadie at piano, and says she herself plays by ear and does not read.

segments.title: Growing up in Pensacola: bands and early jazz
segments.summary: Born in Mariana, Florida, Billie was raised in Pensacola and recalls the Douglas and Joe Jesse orchestras, the instrumentation and jazz there.

segments.title: Pensacola dance halls and water parks
segments.summary: Halls in winter, parks and bath-house dance floors on the water in summer.

segments.title: Visiting New Orleans bands and slipping out to dances
segments.summary: New Orleans bands came to Pensacola; Billie and a sister sneaked out to dances while their father slept, with Sadie playing.

segments.title: Mac Merrimakers and the Mac bandleaders
segments.summary: Sadie and Billie worked with trumpeter Thomas Mac, a New Orleans man who stayed in Pensacola, and Billie worked with the Mac Merrimakers at the Belmont Theater.

segments.title: Which sisters played and with whom
segments.summary: Billie goes through Edna, Mabel, Della, Sadie and Ida, who played church, house parties or bands, plus Ida's musician son.

segments.title: De De's birth certificate and the Pierces' marriage license
segments.summary: Allen reads the 1935 marriage license and De De's 1904 birth record.

segments.title: Photographs of Pensacola and the Makers club
segments.summary: They look at photos of De De and Billie in Pensacola and with violinist Manuel Roberts, with dating guesses.

segments.title: Photograph of a rehearsal with Crawford and Allen present
segments.summary: Allen identifies players in a photo taken at an apartment rehearsal and they joke about a rehearsal night.

segments.title: Photograph of the French Quarter nightclub
segments.summary: A photo of the club Billie worked in the French Quarter, which De De says was painted by a sailor.

segments.title: First tunes Billie learned
segments.summary: She recalls early tunes like Bells That Ring for Me and My Gal and the blues, and her sister playing Keller's Love at home.

segments.title: Coconut Island and the Coconut Grove theme song
segments.summary: Billie explains how Coconut Island became her theme song at the Coconut Grove.

segments.chapter: Touring Alabama and Florida, first New Orleans trips
segments.title: Playing solo and on the Madisonville boat
segments.summary: Billie worked with Mac but also solo; De De recalls the lake boat, its landings and its favourite number.

segments.chapter: Touring Alabama and Florida, first New Orleans trips
segments.title: Century, Alabama: a wild town
segments.summary: Billie describes Century as a wild town with gambling, moonshine, dancing and houses with piano.

segments.chapter: Touring Alabama and Florida, first New Orleans trips
segments.title: Timeline and touring Alabama towns alone
segments.summary: She dates leaving Pensacola and first coming to New Orleans around 1929 and lists the Alabama towns she played solo.

segments.chapter: Touring Alabama and Florida, first New Orleans trips
segments.title: Nighthawk Orchestra in Birmingham and the Mac bands
segments.summary: She names the Birmingham Nighthawk Orchestra, a nine-piece band, and other bands she worked in.

segments.chapter: Touring Alabama and Florida, first New Orleans trips
segments.title: First New Orleans job: Rialto with Lawrence Toca
segments.summary: Filling in for Sadie in 1929, Billie played with Lawrence Toca and Alphonse Picou at the Rialto before going back to Birmingham.

segments.chapter: Touring Alabama and Florida, first New Orleans trips
segments.title: Sadie's boat band and a Mandeville job
segments.summary: Billie struggles to recall the band personnel and tells how Buddy Manaday and Lawrence Toca took her to a Saturday dance in Mandeville.

segments.chapter: Touring Alabama and Florida, first New Orleans trips
segments.title: Back in Pensacola with Mac: Florida tours and personnel
segments.summary: After a year in Birmingham Billie toured Florida towns with Mac's six-piece band, including a Christmas back-and-forth run.

segments.chapter: Touring Alabama and Florida, first New Orleans trips
segments.title: Returning to New Orleans in 1930 and the Madisonville boat band
segments.summary: De De took Buddy Petit's place on the boat; they recall Reuben Oliver, the Nelsons and Willis.

segments.title: About two years at the Rialto and the history of Luchenbach's
segments.summary: Billie stayed two years at the Rialto, then describes Luchenbach's old folks home restaurant and dance hall.

segments.title: Billie's band at Luchenbach's and the Kingfish
segments.summary: Billie led the band with George Lewis, McGee and Boyd and had been at the Kingfish before.

segments.title: How Billie and De De got together and married
segments.summary: Billie tells how she told De De she liked him and how they married about 24 years ago, then travelled with Ida Cox.

segments.title: Billie's sisters as singers and blues
segments.summary: The sisters all sang; Edna, Della and Billie loved blues while Sadie and Ida preferred sentimental songs.

segments.title: Piano players in New Orleans when Billie arrived
segments.summary: They discuss Williamena Bartlett, Jeanette, Edna Francis and Walter Decou, who played ragtime, blues and Spanish pieces.

segments.title: Decatur Street night spots
segments.summary: They list the clubs on Decatur Street where they worked, including Popeye's, the Kingfish and a Filipino place.

segments.title: Decatur Street crowds, celebrities and floor shows
segments.summary: Allen asks who came there; De De and Billie describe sailors, celebrities and shows with dancers like Annabella.

segments.title: Moving to St. Claude and St. Bernard, then Bunkie
segments.summary: After Decatur Street she worked a night spot with floor shows, went to Bunkie for about a year, then back to Luchenbach's.

segments.title: Floor-show tunes and comedians
segments.summary: They played fast numbers for shows; Pokechop and Yeah Man were the comedians.

segments.title: Milton Shots at the Kingfish firing and rehiring Billie
segments.summary: Billie tells how the Kingfish owner fired her, how she nearly quit over no rests, and the low pay.

segments.title: Playing across the street and drinking on the job
segments.summary: De De recalls staying on while Billie joined the Filipino band, and the drinking on the bandstand.

segments.title: The St. Bernard trio and who went to Bunkie
segments.summary: Billie lists the three-piece group, then the musicians she took to Bunkie, including Kid Ernest and Frank Gibbs.

segments.title: Piron, the violinist and Steve Lewis at the Pelican
segments.summary: Neighbours Piron and the Mexican-looking violinist come up, then Billie recalls playing with Steve Lewis at the Pelican.

segments.title: Back to Luchenbach's with Big Eye Louie and Rodgers
segments.summary: Back at Luchenbach's she had Big Eye Louie Nelson and Rodgers, and Octave Crosby; they try to recall a pianist.

segments.title: Smiley starting out as an entertainer at the Kingfish
segments.summary: They started a dancer who played ukulele at the Kingfish by pushing him onto the floor.

segments.title: The Absinthe Bar with Piron, and the Cave
segments.summary: Billie and De De played short jobs at the Absinthe Bar with Piron and Walter Pichon, and at the Cave.

segments.title: 24 years at Luchenbach's and going to Bunkie in the war
segments.summary: Billie says she stayed at Luchenbach's about 24 years and went to Bunkie during the war.

segments.title: De De's birth and family
segments.summary: De De was born in New Orleans in 1904; no one in his family played music; they look at family photos.

segments.title: De De's teacher Charlot and his influences
segments.summary: He learned his notes from Charlot, a letter carrier, was influenced by Rene and Chris Kelly, and picked up mute playing himself.

segments.title: De De's first job and forming his own band
segments.summary: He got his first job replacing Cuckoo in a drummer's band, then branched out and formed his own groups.

segments.title: De De as extra trumpet in other men's bands
segments.summary: He was hired out as second trumpet to Rene, Buddy and others, and describes how the bands mixed.

segments.title: De De's favourite trumpet players
segments.summary: Rene was his favourite, followed by Guy Kelly; they discuss Punch.

segments.title: De De's French Quarter jobs
segments.summary: He worked many spots on Decatur Street near the river.

segments.title: Working with Celestin
segments.summary: De De worked with Celestin for a while; Celestin liked a woman on piano.

segments.title: De De's band with Paul Barnes
segments.summary: About 30 years ago he played with Paul Barnes; he names the saxophonists and second trumpet.

segments.title: How the Alligator Bar song began
segments.summary: De De tells how a Creole joke at the race track became a song.

segments.title: Coconut Grove nightclub advertisement
segments.summary: Allen reads a Coconut Grove ad at 300 Burgundy Street; they date it around 1947 and Allen gives the date of the interview.

segments.title: Billie at the Harmony Inn with Mealy
segments.summary: After Rodgers she worked at the Harmony Inn with Mealy, Lawrence Toca and a drummer for about a year.

segments.title: The River Bell
segments.summary: They worked the River Bell with Mealy and George Henry, and a white band later replaced them.

segments.title: Mealy's drinking and the fire
segments.summary: They joke about Mealy's whiskey and recall a New Year's fire.

segments.title: Billie's first records
segments.summary: Billie recalls the first record session upstairs, with Albert Jiles, Mealy and others, for Alden and David's label.

segments.title: De De's first records and the Paul Barnes broadcast
segments.summary: De De cannot recall his first record and says Paul Barnes did radio broadcasts from Lake Charles.

segments.title: Playing with Don Albert and Arthur Durbin's breakdown
segments.summary: De De recalls a Texas trip with Don Albert's big band, then Arthur Durbin losing his mind on the bandstand.

segments.title: Playing for Bessie Smith in Pensacola
segments.summary: Billie played Gulf Coast Blues for Bessie Smith in Pensacola when Clarence Williams came through.

segments.title: Singers Billie admired
segments.summary: Billie says Ida Cox and Bessie were her favourites, and she did not care for Ma Rainey.

segments.title: On the road with Ida Cox
segments.summary: About twelve years earlier Billie went on the road with Ida Cox, picking up musicians near Biloxi.

segments.title: Aside about thieves and the table
segments.summary: An aside about people stealing things, then Allen turns to Ernest.

segments.title: Introducing Ernest Silver Trepagnier
segments.summary: Allen records Silver Trepagnier's age, birth in 1899 and WPA work.

segments.title: Ernest's in-laws Frank Crump and Henry Julian
segments.summary: He names his musical brothers-in-law, Frank Crump's death and Ernest Crump on banjo.

segments.title: Ernest's violin lessons and banjo
segments.summary: He started violin lessons in 1910, later got a banjo, and recalls early pieces.

segments.title: Bands Ernest remembers
segments.summary: He recalls Piron's band, Emmanuel Perez and Joe Oliver.

segments.title: De De's first brass band with Gunye
segments.summary: De De recalls his cousin Dejean's brass band, its members, music and marching tempos.

segments.title: Funeral marches and returning from the cemetery
segments.summary: Funeral marches, hymns and the jazz after the burial.

segments.title: Playing for Louis Armstrong as king of the Zulus and the Secret Nine
segments.summary: De De recalls the brass band for Armstrong's Zulu parade and a baseball ceremony at the boys' home.

segments.title: Ernest on second lining
segments.summary: Ernest followed bands as a boy; they discuss banjo and bass in parades.

segments.title: Dance halls Ernest attended
segments.summary: Ernest lists dance halls such as Artesian Hall and Economy Hall.

segments.title: Closing the tape
segments.summary: Allen ends because the tape is nearly out.
